      <div class="space-y-8 max-w-4xl mx-auto">
        <div class="text-center space-y-2">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent">Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">Answers to critical questions regarding Connecticut Workers' Compensation.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="space-y-4">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Is Workers' Compensation mandatory for small businesses in Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Yes. Under the Connecticut Workers' Compensation Act (CGS § 31-284), any business that employs one or more individuals—regardless of whether they are full-time, part-time, seasonal, or family members—must maintain active workers' compensation insurance. Failure to do so can result in state-issued stop-work orders and civil fines starting at $500 per day.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Can business owners or LLC members exclude themselves from Workers' Comp coverage?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Yes. Sole proprietors, single-member LLCs, and corporate officers in Connecticut have the legal option to exclude themselves from coverage using state Form 6B or Form 75 to reduce premium costs. However, if they hire even one part-time assistant or apprentice, they must purchase a policy covering that employee.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What is a 'Ghost Policy' in Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              A 'Ghost Policy' (or minimum premium policy) is an affordable workers' compensation policy purchased by a self-employed sole proprietor or independent contractor with zero employees. It provides a valid Certificate of Insurance (COI) to satisfy general contractor or client contract mandates without paying for unnecessary payroll coverage.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">How does the annual Workers' Compensation payroll audit work?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              At policy expiration, your insurance carrier compares your estimated payroll against your actual state wage filings (Forms CT-941 and W-2/1099s). If your payroll was higher or if subcontractors lacked certificates, you receive an adjustment bill. Associated Insurance Agency works with you throughout the policy term to adjust payroll declarations and verify classification codes so you avoid unexpected audit bills.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

              01
            </div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Qué es un Certificado ACORD 25?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              El ACORD 25 es el formato estándar reconocido en EE.UU. que resume los números de póliza, aseguradoras, fechas de vigencia y límites de Responsabilidad General, Auto Comercial y Compensación de Trabajadores.
            </p>

          <div class="p-6 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle bg-white shadow-xs space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 text-accent flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-base">
              02
            </div>

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            </p>

            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 text-accent flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-base">
              03
            </div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Renuncia de Subrogación</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Prohíbe a la compañía de seguros reclamar legalmente el reembolso al titular del certificado tras indemnizar un siniestro, protegiendo las relaciones comerciales entre subcontratistas y clientes.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="p-6 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle bg-white shadow-xs space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-xl bg-accent/10 text-accent flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-base">
              04
            </div>

En caso de accidente grave, la aseguradora personal rechazará el reclamo, dejando a su empresa expuesta a demandas multimillonarias.
            </p>

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Qué es el seguro de Auto Alquilado y No Propio (HNOA)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              La cobertura HNOA protege a su empresa cuando sus empleados utilizan sus propios autos personales para realizar tareas de la compañía (ir al banco, buscar materiales o visitar clientes) o cuando alquila vehículos temporalmente. Si causan un accidente, esta cobertura protege su empresa una vez agotados los límites del empleado.
            </p>

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Las pólizas comerciales estándar cubren el vehículo físico y los accesorios fijos, pero no las herramientas sueltas o maquinaria transportada. Para proteger herramientas manuales, generadores o materiales, AIA incluye un endoso de 'Inland Marine' o seguro de equipo móvil.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Qué límites de responsabilidad civil deben tener los vehículos comerciales en CT?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Aunque los mínimos estatales de Connecticut (CGS § 14-112) son de solo $25k/$50k/$25k, son insuficientes para empresas. La mayoría de los vehículos de trabajo y flotas aseguran límites combinados (CSL) de $500,000 a $1,000,000, frecuentemente complementados con un Paraguas Comercial.
            </p>

          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">02</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Daños Materiales a Terceros</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Paga los costos de reparación o reemplazo si usted o sus empleados dañan accidentalmente la propiedad de un cliente durante el trabajo.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">03</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Productos y Operaciones Terminadas</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Protege su empresa después de concluir el trabajo. Si una instalación falla o un producto comercializado causa daños semanas después, esta cobertura responde.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Responsabilidad por Publicidad y Calumnia</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Protección legal frente a demandas por infracción de derechos de autor en anuncios publicitarios, calumnia o competencia desleal involuntaria.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">05</div>

            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Defensa Legal y Honorarios</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            </p>

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Es obligatorio por ley el seguro de Responsabilidad Civil General en Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Aunque los estatutos de Connecticut no exigen universalmente la responsabilidad civil general para todas las empresas, es prácticamente indispensable. Los arrendadores comerciales la exigen para firmar contratos de alquiler, las agencias municipales y contratistas generales solicitan pruebas de cobertura (COI) antes de otorgar obras, y las juntas de licencias de oficios exigen pólizas vigentes.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Con qué rapidez puede Associated Insurance Agency emitir un Certificado de Seguro (COI)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Para asegurados activos, Associated Insurance Agency emite Certificados de Seguro estándar ACORD 25 el mismo día, frecuentemente en cuestión de minutos. Esto permite a los contratistas licitar trabajos, ingresar a sitios de construcción y cumplir con los requisitos del cliente sin retrasos.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              El estándar de referencia para responsabilidad general comercial en Connecticut es de $1,000,000 por incidente y $2,000,000 acumulado general ($1M/$2M). Contratistas de mayor riesgo o empresas que realizan obras públicas suelen adquirir pólizas Paraguas Comercial para elevar los límites a $5,000,000 o más.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cuál es la diferencia entre una póliza de Responsabilidad General independiente y una BOP?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Una póliza independiente solo cubre reclamos de terceros por lesiones y daños materiales. Una Póliza para Propietarios de Negocios (BOP) combina la Responsabilidad General con el Seguro de Propiedad Comercial y la Pérdida de Ingresos en un solo paquete con tarifa reducida, ideal para pequeños comercios y oficinas.
            </p>
          </div>

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

Según la Ley de Compensación de Trabajadores de Connecticut (CGS § 31-284), cualquier empresa con uno o más empleados (ya sean de tiempo completo, medio tiempo o estacionales) debe contar con seguro de compensación de trabajadores. No cumplir con la ley conlleva órdenes de paralización inmediata y multas estatales de al menos $500 por día.

En AIA le ayudamos a clasificar adecuadamente a su personal para evitar cobros sorpresa al final del año.

Si causa un choque con varios heridos o destruye un auto reciente, las cuentas médicas y de taller superan el mínimo estatal con rapidez.           </h3>

          </p>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            </p>

            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cuáles son los límites mínimos obligatorios de seguro de auto en Connecticut (CGS § 14-112)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Bajo la ley de Connecticut (CGS § 14-112), todo conductor debe portar una cobertura mínima de responsabilidad civil de $25,000 por lesiones por persona, $50,000 por accidente en total y $25,000 por daños a la propiedad (25/50/25), además de cobertura equivalente para conductores sin seguro o con seguro insuficiente (UM/UIM).
            </p>

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              El precio promedio de un auto nuevo supera los $48,000. Si causa un choque que destruye un auto reciente, el límite estatal de $25,000 deja una diferencia de más de $20,000 que saldrá de su propio bolsillo. Si los gastos médicos de los lesionados superan los $50,000 de su póliza, pueden demandar sus cuentas de ahorro y su vivienda. Recomendamos contratar límites de al menos 100/300/100 o 250/500/100.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cuál es la diferencia entre cobertura de Colisión e Integral en Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              La cobertura de Colisión paga la reparación o reemplazo de su propio auto si choca contra otro vehículo, un poste o patina en hielo. La cobertura Integral cubre daños ajenos a una colisión: impacto con venados en carreteras rurales, piedras en el parabrisas, robo, vandalismo, incendio y ramas caídas por tormentas.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Puedo asegurar una casa rodante, cámper o remolque en la misma póliza?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              La mayoría de las aseguradoras requieren una póliza especializada para vehículos recreativos en vez de añadirlos a una póliza de auto estándar. Podemos emitir ambas pólizas con la misma compañía para aprovechar descuentos y cubrir responsabilidad en campamentos, remolque y pertenencias personales.

También incluye cobertura de responsabilidad civil si un invitado se lesiona en su propiedad.

Associated Insurance Agency trabaja con aseguradoras como Travelers, Safeco, Hanover y Liberty Mutual para ajustar la cobertura al costo real de reconstrucción de su vivienda.

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cuál es la diferencia entre el costo de reemplazo y el valor de mercado?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              El valor de mercado es lo que un comprador paga por su casa, incluyendo el terreno y el vecindario. El costo de reconstrucción es el costo de materiales y mano de obra necesario para rehacer la vivienda desde cero. En Connecticut, los costos de construcción y mano de obra están entre los más altos del país, por lo que el costo de reconstrucción suele ser muy diferente del valor de tasación inmobiliaria.
            </p>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cubre el seguro de hogar de Connecticut los daños por congelación de tuberías y acumulación de hielo?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Sí. Las pólizas estándar HO-3 y HO-5 generalmente cubren tuberías rotas por frío y filtraciones por presas de hielo en el techo, siempre que se haya mantenido la calefacción en la vivienda. Sin embargo, los daños por agua de alcantarillado o drenajes requieren un endoso adicional.
            </p>

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Están cubiertas las inundaciones en una póliza de propietarios estándar?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              No. El seguro de propietarios excluye inundaciones por agua de lluvia en superficie, desbordamiento de ríos o marejadas ciclónicas. La cobertura contra inundaciones requiere una póliza independiente del Programa Nacional de Seguros contra Inundaciones (NFIP) o de aseguradoras privadas, la cual podemos emitir junto con su póliza de hogar.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">¿Cuánto puedo ahorrar al combinar seguro de auto y casa en Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Al combinar sus pólizas de hogar y auto con la misma aseguradora a través de Associated Insurance Agency, normalmente obtiene descuentos de entre el 15% y el 25% en ambas primas, unifica su facturación y simplifica la gestión de reclamos.

            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

Las demandas judiciales no afectan únicamente a familias adineradas. Los factores de riesgo más habituales incluyen conductores jóvenes, piscinas, perros y propiedades en alquiler.

              <a href="/es/quote?type=renters" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-accent-gold hover:text-accent-gold-hover transition-colors">
                Solicitar Cotización de Inquilinos
                <svg class="w-4 h-4" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
                  <path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M13.5 4.5 21 12m0 0-7.5 7.5M21 12H3" />
                </svg>
              </a>
              <a href="/es/personal/renters" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-xs font-semibold text-accent hover:underline">
                Explorar Guía de Inquilinos y Preguntas Frecuentes →
              </a>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="lg:col-span-8 bg-bg-secondary p-8 rounded-lg border border-border-subtle space-y-6">
            <div class="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-6 text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              <div>
                <h4 class="font-bold text-text-primary mb-1">Seguro de Inquilinos</h4>
                <p>Cubre el reemplazo de ropa, computadoras y muebles en caso de robo o incendio. Incluye responsabilidad civil del inquilino en caso de accidentes menores dentro de la unidad alquilada.</p>
              </div>
              <div>
                <h4 class="font-bold text-text-primary mb-1">Seguro para Mascotas</h4>
                <p>Planes de accidentes y enfermedades para perros y gatos. Cubre visitas veterinarias, cirugías y recetas médicas para que nunca tenga que tomar decisiones de salud basadas en el costo.</p>
              </div>
            </div>

            <h2 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Nuestro Compromiso con su Privacidad</h2>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              <strong>Associated Insurance Agency</strong> ("AIA", "nosotros" o "nuestro") valora su confianza. Como agencia de seguros independiente que opera en Danbury, Watertown y Bridgeport, Connecticut, gestionamos información personal y financiera necesaria para obtener cotizaciones, emitir coberturas y administrar pólizas. Nunca vendemos sus datos personales ni números móviles a comercializadores externos o listas de telemercadeo.
            </p>

          <!-- Sección 1 -->
          <article id="vision-general" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 1</span>
              Visión General y Aviso de la Ley Gramm-Leach-Bliley (GLBA)
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Esta Política de Privacidad describe cómo Associated Insurance Agency recopila, utiliza, resguarda y divulga información personal e información financiera personal no pública (NPI) a través de nuestro sitio web (<a href="https://aia-danbury.com/es" class="text-accent underline font-medium">https://aia-danbury.com/es</a>), cotizadores en línea, llamadas telefónicas y consultas presenciales.
            </p>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Conforme al Título V de la Ley Gramm-Leach-Bliley (GLBA) y las regulaciones del Departamento de Seguros de Connecticut, las instituciones financieras y agencias de seguros autorizadas están obligadas a informar sus políticas y prácticas de privacidad a los consumidores.
            </p>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 2 -->
          <article id="informacion-recopilada" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 2</span>
              Información que Recopilamos
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Para evaluar el riesgo de seguro y solicitar propuestas precisas a las compañías aseguradoras, recopilamos las siguientes categorías de datos:
            </p>
            <div class="space-y-2.5 text-xs text-text-secondary">
              <div class="p-3 bg-bg-secondary rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
                <strong class="text-text-primary block mb-0.5">Datos de Contacto</strong>
                Nombre completo, dirección residencial y postal, correo electrónico, números telefónicos y oficina de preferencia.
              </div>
              <div class="p-3 bg-bg-secondary rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
                <strong class="text-text-primary block mb-0.5">Datos de Seguros y Suscripción</strong>
                Número de identificación del vehículo (VIN), historial de conducción, antigüedad y características de la propiedad, acreedores hipotecarios, aseguradora anterior y registros de reclamos.
              </div>
              <div class="p-3 bg-bg-secondary rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
                <strong class="text-text-primary block mb-0.5">Información Comercial</strong>
                Nombre comercial, identificación fiscal patronal (FEIN), nómina, ventas brutas, ubicaciones operativas y clasificaciones de negocio.
              </div>
              <div class="p-3 bg-bg-secondary rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
                <strong class="text-text-primary block mb-0.5">Datos Técnicos y de Seguridad</strong>
                Direcciones IP, navegador, sistema operativo, fecha/hora y parámetros de seguridad honeypot para mitigar envíos de bots automatizados.
              </div>
            </div>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 3: Confidencialidad Móvil Estricta (10DLC / CTIA) -->
          <article id="privacidad-movil" class="space-y-4 scroll-mt-28 p-6 bg-accent/5 border border-accent/20 rounded-xl">

              </svg>
              <div>
                <h2 class="text-lg font-bold text-accent">
                  Sección 3: Confidencialidad Estricta de Telefonía Móvil y Mensajes SMS (10DLC / CTIA)
                </h2>
                <div class="mt-2 p-3 bg-white border border-border-subtle rounded-lg text-sm text-text-primary font-medium leading-relaxed">
                  "No se compartirá información móvil con terceros o afiliados con fines de marketing o promocionales. Todas las demás categorías excluyen los datos de suscripción y consentimiento del originador de mensajes de texto; esta información no se compartirá con ningún tercero."
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              En nuestros formularios en línea, nuestro aviso indica: <em>"Proporcionar un número permite llamadas/mensajes de texto de nuestra parte sobre el mensaje."</em>
            </p>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Su número de teléfono celular y el consentimiento para SMS son utilizados <strong>exclusivamente</strong> por Associated Insurance Agency para comunicarse directamente con usted con relación a su solicitud de cotización, servicio de póliza o renovaciones. Jamás vendemos, alquilamos ni cedemos su número ni el consentimiento de suscripción a terceros o redes de comercialización.
            </p>
            <ul class="space-y-1 text-xs text-text-secondary pl-5 list-disc">
              <li>Puede cancelar las comunicaciones por SMS en cualquier momento respondiendo <strong>STOP</strong>.</li>
              <li>Responda <strong>HELP</strong> para obtener asistencia o información de servicio al cliente.</li>
            </ul>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 4 -->
          <article id="uso-informacion" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 4</span>
              Cómo Usamos su Información
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Utilizamos los datos recopilados estrictamente para operaciones legítimas de correduría de seguros:
            </p>
            <ul class="space-y-2 text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary pl-5 list-disc">
              <li><strong>Comparación de Tarifas:</strong> Enviar los datos preliminares a aseguradoras líderes autorizadas para comparar precios y pólizas.</li>
              <li><strong>Servicio de Pólizas:</strong> Asistir en la adición de vehículos o conductores, expedición de certificados (COI) y consultas de facturación.</li>
              <li><strong>Comunicación Directa:</strong> Contactarlo por teléfono, correo electrónico, mensaje de texto o correo postal sobre sus cotizaciones o pólizas activas.</li>
              <li><strong>Prevención de Fraudes:</strong> Proteger nuestros sistemas contra envíos automatizados no deseados y solicitudes maliciosas.</li>
              <li><strong>Cumplimiento Legal:</strong> Cumplir con las normativas y requerimientos del Departamento de Seguros de Connecticut.</li>
            </ul>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 5 -->
          <article id="divulgacion-aseguradoras" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 5</span>
              Divulgación y Compartición de Información
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Como agencia independiente, AIA comparte sus datos únicamente con las partes necesarias para procesar sus trámites de seguros:
            </p>
            <ul class="space-y-2 text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary pl-5 list-disc">
              <li><strong>Compañías Aseguradoras:</strong> Para cotizar, evaluar el riesgo y emitir pólizas (Safeco, Travelers, Progressive, The Hartford, Foremost, Guard, etc.).</li>
              <li><strong>Agencias de Informes del Consumidor:</strong> Las aseguradoras pueden solicitar reportes de manejo (MVR) e historial de reclamos (C.L.U.E.).</li>
              <li><strong>Proveedores de Tecnología:</strong> Empresas que alojan nuestros sistemas de gestión de pólizas bajo estrictos acuerdos de confidencialidad.</li>
              <li><strong>Autoridades Gubernamentales:</strong> En respuesta a órdenes judiciales o requerimientos del Departamento de Seguros de Connecticut.</li>
            </ul>
            <p class="text-xs font-semibold text-accent pt-1">
              NO VENDEMOS NI ALQUILAMOS SU INFORMACIÓN PERSONAL A TERCEROS PARA PUBLICIDAD COMERCIAL.
            </p>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 6 -->
          <article id="cookies-registros" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 6</span>
              Cookies y Registros Técnicos
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Nuestro sitio web utiliza cookies de sesión estándar y mecanismos de seguridad para garantizar una navegación fluida y evitar formularios falsos. No utilizamos píxeles invasivos ni rastreadores de perfiles de terceros con fines publicitarios.
            </p>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 7 -->
          <article id="seguridad-datos" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 7</span>
              Medidas de Seguridad y Protección de Datos
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              AIA implementa medidas de seguridad físicas, electrónicas y de procedimiento de conformidad con los estándares de la ley GLBA y la Ley de Privacidad de Datos de Connecticut (CTDPA). Esto incluye cifrado SSL/TLS, cortafuegos y acceso restringido exclusivo para agentes autorizados.
            </p>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 8 -->
          <article id="retencion-datos" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
              <span class="text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded bg-accent/10 text-accent">Sección 8</span>
              Requisitos de Retención de Documentos
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Las agencias de seguros están sujetas a normas estatales y federales de conservación de registros. Conservamos expedientes de asegurados, solicitudes y comunicaciones durante los períodos exigidos por la ley estatal (generalmente entre 5 y 7 años tras el vencimiento o cancelación de la póliza).
            </p>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 9 -->
          <article id="derechos-usuario" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">

              Sus Derechos de Privacidad
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Conforme a la legislación aplicable y sujeto a los requisitos de archivo regulatorio, usted tiene derecho a:
            </p>
            <ul class="space-y-1.5 text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary pl-5 list-disc">
              <li>Solicitar acceso para revisar los datos personales en su expediente activo.</li>
              <li>Solicitar la corrección de datos incorrectos o desactualizados.</li>
              <li>Darse de baja de comunicaciones comerciales (respondiendo STOP o mediante enlaces de correo).</li>
            </ul>
          </article>

          <!-- Sección 10 -->
          <article id="privacidad-menores" class="space-y-3 scroll-mt-28">
            <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">

              Privacidad de Menores (COPPA)
            </h2>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Este sitio está destinado a adultos y propietarios de empresas. No recopilamos conscientemente información de menores de 13 años. Si cree que un menor nos ha provisto datos, comuníquese con nosotros para eliminarlos inmediatamente.

            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

Como agencia independiente, AIA representa a múltiples compañías aseguradoras terceras (incluyendo Safeco, Travelers, Progressive, The Hartford, Foremost, entre otras).
            </p>

Todas las pólizas, coberturas, endosos, tarifas, exclusiones, resoluciones de reclamos y cancelaciones se rigen estrictamente por los contratos de póliza emitidos por las respectivas aseguradoras suscriptoras.

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

La cobertura solo entra en vigencia una vez que un agente de seguros con licencia autorizado haya confirmado directamente por escrito su emisión o modificación, y el pago inicial obligatorio haya sido procesado por la compañía aseguradora correspondiente.

      <div class="grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-12 gap-10 items-start">
        <div class="lg:col-span-7 space-y-5">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent tracking-tight">
            Connecticut Auto Insurance Mandates (CGS § 14-112)
          </h2>
          <div class="p-4 bg-accent/5 border-l-4 border-accent-gold rounded-r text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
              Connecticut law requires every motor vehicle owner to maintain financial responsibility with minimum liability limits of $25,000 bodily injury per person, $50,000 per accident, and $25,000 property damage (25/50/25), plus matching Uninsured and Underinsured Motorist (UM/UIM) protection.
            </p>
          </div>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Meeting that minimum lets you legally register a car with the DMV, but $25,000 in property damage does not even cover the replacement cost of an average vehicle on Connecticut roads today. If you cause an accident with multiple injuries or total a newer car, repair and medical bills exceed state minimums fast. Any balance beyond your policy limits comes out of your own pocket.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="lg:col-span-5 bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-4">
          <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">
            Why 25/50/25 Limits Put Your Assets at Risk
          </h3>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            The average new car sold today costs over $48,000. If your property damage cap is $25,000, you are personally liable for the rest.
          </p>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            If damages exceed your policy, the other driver's attorney can pursue your personal bank accounts, place liens on your home, or garnish future wages under Connecticut court judgments. Stepping up to 100/300/100 or 250/500/100 liability usually adds only a modest amount to your monthly bill while protecting your assets.
          </p>
        </div>

          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">A breakdown of mandatory liability and physical damage protections.</p>

        <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">

            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">01</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Bodily Injury Liability</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pays medical expenses, rehabilitation, and legal representation when you are at fault in an accident causing injury to other drivers or pedestrians.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">02</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Property Damage Liability</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pays to repair or replace vehicles, guardrails, utility poles, or buildings damaged in an accident where you are at fault.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">03</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Collision Coverage</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pays to repair or replace your car if you hit another vehicle, slide off an icy road into a guardrail, or roll over, minus your deductible.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">04</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Comprehensive Coverage</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pays for damage from hazards other than crashes: hitting a deer on a rural backroad, stone chips on the windshield, theft, vandalism, storm flooding, and fallen tree branches.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">05</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Uninsured / Underinsured Motorist (UM/UIM)</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Protects you and your passengers if struck by an uninsured driver, a hit-and-run motorist, or a driver whose policy limits fall short of your medical bills.
            </p>

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What are Connecticut's mandatory auto insurance minimums (CGS § 14-112)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Under Connecticut General Statutes (CGS § 14-112), registered drivers must carry liability coverage of at least $25,000 bodily injury per person, $50,000 total bodily injury per accident, and $25,000 property damage (25/50/25), along with matching Uninsured and Underinsured Motorist (UM/UIM) coverage.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Why are Connecticut state minimum limits inadequate for most drivers?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              New vehicles in Connecticut now average around $48,000. If you cause a crash that totals a late-model car, a $25,000 property damage cap leaves a $23,000 gap that you have to pay out of pocket. If medical expenses for other passengers exceed your $50,000 bodily injury limit, injured parties can seek judgments against your personal savings and real estate. We recommend carrying at least 100/300/100 or 250/500/100 in liability.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What is the difference between Collision and Comprehensive coverage in Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Collision pays to repair or replace your vehicle when you hit another vehicle, hit a fixed object like a guardrail or tree, or roll over. Comprehensive covers damage from incidents outside a crash: hitting a deer or wild animal, windshield chips and cracks, theft, vandalism, fire, and branches knocked down during storms.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Can I insure my RV, camper, or travel trailer on the same policy?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Most carriers require a dedicated recreational vehicle policy rather than adding an RV directly to a standard auto policy. We can bundle both policies with the same carrier or place your RV with a specialized insurer to cover campsite liability, roadside towing, and contents replacement.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>

    <div class="max-w-7xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 space-y-20">

      <!-- What is Homeowners / Answer Framing Snippet -->
      <div class="grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-12 gap-10 items-start">
        <div class="lg:col-span-7 space-y-5">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent tracking-tight">
            What Does Homeowners Insurance Cover in Connecticut?
          </h2>
          <div class="p-4 bg-accent/5 border-l-4 border-accent-gold rounded-r text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
              Connecticut homeowners insurance pays to repair or rebuild your home and replace personal belongings after damage from fire, lightning, wind, hail, heavy snow, or vandalism. It also includes liability coverage if a guest is injured on your property.
            </p>
          </div>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Homes in Western Connecticut range from older houses in Litchfield County to coastal properties in Fairfield County, each with different rebuilding costs and storm risks. Associated Insurance Agency works with carriers including Travelers, Safeco, Hanover, and Liberty Mutual to match coverage to your home's actual rebuild value.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="lg:col-span-5 bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-4">
          <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent flex items-center gap-2">
            <span class="w-2 h-2 rounded-full bg-accent-gold"></span>
            Replacement Cost vs. Market Value
          </h3>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            Many homeowners base their coverage on purchase price or town tax assessments. What matters instead is dwelling replacement cost: the actual price of materials and local contractor labor needed to rebuild from scratch.
          </p>
          <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
            We calculate coverage using regional rebuilding cost indexes and offer extended replacement cost endorsements (up to 125% to 150%) so sharp spikes in material costs do not leave you short after a major claim.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <!-- Core Coverage Grid -->
      <div class="space-y-8">
        <div class="text-center max-w-2xl mx-auto space-y-2">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent">Standard Policy Coverage (HO-3 & HO-5)</h2>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">How HO-3 and HO-5 policies break down essential protections.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">A</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage A: Dwelling</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pays to repair or rebuild your home's physical structure, including the foundation, roof, walls, and built-in appliances, after fire, wind, or storm damage.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">B</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage B: Other Structures</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Covers detached structures on your property, including garages, sheds, fences, driveways, and pools.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">C</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage C: Personal Property</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pays to replace furniture, clothing, electronics, and household goods if they are damaged, destroyed, or stolen at home or while traveling.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">D</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage D: Loss of Use</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pays temporary living costs (such as hotel stays, short-term rentals, meals, and storage) if covered damage makes your home unlivable during repairs.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">E</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage E: Personal Liability</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Covers legal defense costs and settlements if a guest is injured on your property or you accidentally damage someone else's property.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-3">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-accent/10 flex items-center justify-center text-accent font-bold text-sm">F</div>
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-text-primary">Coverage F: Medical Payments</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Covers medical bills for guests injured on your property, regardless of fault, helping handle minor accidents without legal claims.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <!-- Critical Connecticut Endorsements -->
      <div class="bg-bg-secondary p-8 sm:p-10 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle space-y-6">
        <div class="max-w-2xl space-y-2">
          <h2 class="text-2xl sm:text-3xl font-bold text-accent">Essential Connecticut Policy Endorsements</h2>
          <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary">
            Standard policies contain specific exclusions. We recommend these riders to cover common local hazards:
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-4 text-xs">
          <div class="bg-white p-4 rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
            <strong class="text-accent block mb-1">Water Backup & Sump Overflow</strong>
            <p class="text-text-muted">Covers water damage to finished basements and living areas from backed-up drains, sewers, or failed sump pumps.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="bg-white p-4 rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
            <strong class="text-accent block mb-1">Service Line Protection</strong>
            <p class="text-text-muted">Covers excavation and repair costs when underground water, sewer, or power lines break on your property.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="bg-white p-4 rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
            <strong class="text-accent block mb-1">Equipment Breakdown</strong>
            <p class="text-text-muted">Covers sudden mechanical or electrical failure of heating systems, AC compressors, heat pumps, and electrical panels.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="bg-white p-4 rounded-lg border border-border-subtle">
            <strong class="text-accent block mb-1">Scheduled Valuables (Floaters)</strong>
            <p class="text-text-muted">Provides agreed-value, zero-deductible coverage for jewelry, watches, art, and collections that exceed standard policy limits.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <!-- New England Climate & Seasonal Exposures -->
      <div class="bg-white p-8 rounded-2xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-4">
        <h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-accent">Built for Connecticut Winters & Nor'easters</h2>
        <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
          Connecticut winters bring specific property risks: sub-zero cold that freezes pipes, heavy snow loads that cause ice dams, and coastal nor'easters that knock oak branches onto roofs and utility lines.
        </p>
        <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
          We help you choose deductibles that fit your budget, connect you directly with claims teams when storms hit, and make sure your policy covers common local winter damage.
        </p>
      </div>

      <!-- FAQ Section -->
      <div class="space-y-8 max-w-4xl mx-auto">
        <div class="text-center space-y-2">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent">Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">Answers to common Connecticut home insurance inquiries.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="space-y-4">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">What is the difference between dwelling replacement cost and market value?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Market value is what a buyer pays for your home, including the land and neighborhood. Dwelling replacement cost is the labor and material cost required to rebuild the house from the ground up. Connecticut has some of the highest construction and labor rates in the country, so rebuild costs often differ substantially from real estate market value or property tax assessments.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Does standard Connecticut homeowners insurance cover winter freeze damage and ice dams?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Yes. Standard HO-3 and HO-5 policies generally cover burst pipes and water damage from roof ice dams, as long as you maintained heat in the home. However, damage from backed-up sewer or drainage lines requires a separate water backup endorsement.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Is flood damage covered under a standard homeowners policy?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              No. Homeowners policies exclude flood damage from rising surface water, overflowing rivers, and coastal storm surges. Flood coverage requires a separate policy through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) or private flood carriers, which Associated Insurance Agency can bind on your behalf.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">How much can I save by bundling home and auto insurance in Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Bundling your home and auto policies with the same insurance carrier usually lowers both premiums by 15% to 25%, puts your coverage on a single billing account, and makes claims easier to coordinate.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

            <h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-accent">Why Do Connecticut Residents Need Personal Umbrella Insurance?</h2>
            <div class="p-3.5 bg-accent/5 border-l-4 border-accent-gold rounded-r text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
                Personal umbrella insurance provides excess liability protection starting at $1,000,000 above standard homeowners and auto policy limits. In severe accidents or premise liability lawsuits, an umbrella policy safeguards your primary home equity, savings accounts, and future earnings from catastrophic judicial judgments, typically for under $300 in annual premium.
              </p>
            </div>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              In our highly litigious society, a single severe auto accident or pool injury on your property can result in judgements exceeding your standard auto or home liability limits. Personal umbrella insurance adds an extra layer of liability protection.
            </p>
            <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3 pt-1">
              <a href="/quote?type=umbrella" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-accent-gold hover:text-accent-gold-hover transition-colors">
                Request Umbrella Quote
                <svg class="w-4 h-4" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
                  <path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M13.5 4.5 21 12m0 0-7.5 7.5M21 12H3" />
                </svg>
              </a>
              <a href="/personal/umbrella" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-xs font-semibold text-accent hover:underline">
                Explore In-Depth Umbrella Guide & FAQs →
              </a>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="lg:col-span-8 bg-bg-secondary p-8 rounded-lg border border-border-subtle space-y-6">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Why Umbrella Matters</h3>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              If your homeowners policy has a $300,000 liability limit, and a guest falls from a deck and sues you for $800,000, you are responsible for the remaining $500,000 out of pocket. That could put your savings, investments, and home equity at risk. 
            </p>
            <p class="text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              An umbrella policy sits on top of your underlying policies (home, auto, boat) and kicks in when their limits are exhausted. Policies typically start at $1 million in additional coverage for around $150 to $300 a year, making it one of the most cost-effective forms of wealth protection available.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Renters & Specialty (RV, Pet) -->
        <div id="renters" class="grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-12 gap-12 pt-12 border-t border-border-subtle">
          <div class="lg:col-span-4 space-y-4">
            <div class="w-10 h-10 rounded bg-accent/5 flex items-center justify-center text-accent">
              <!-- Star/Specialty Icon -->
              <svg class="w-5 h-5" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
                <path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M11.48 3.499c.3-.921 1.603-.921 1.902 0l1.519 4.674a1 1 0 0 0 .95.69h4.915c.969 0 1.371 1.24.588 1.81l-3.976 2.888a1 1 0 0 0-.363 1.118l1.518 4.674c.3.922-.755 1.688-1.538 1.118l-3.976-2.888a1 1 0 0 0-1.176 0l-3.976 2.888c-.783.57-1.838-.197-1.538-1.118l1.518-4.674a1 1 0 0 0-.363-1.118l-3.976-2.888c-.784-.57-.38-1.81.588-1.81h4.914a1 1 0 0 0 .951-.69l1.519-4.674Z" />
              </svg>
            </div>
            <h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-accent">What Does Renters & Specialty Coverage Protect in Connecticut?</h2>
            <div class="p-3.5 bg-accent/5 border-l-4 border-accent-gold rounded-r text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
                While a landlord's policy protects the physical apartment structure, renters insurance safeguards your personal belongings—including electronics, furniture, and clothing—against fire, theft, and water leaks, while providing personal liability protection. AIA also secures specialized policies for recreational vehicles (motorhomes, boats) and comprehensive veterinary pet insurance across Connecticut.
              </p>
            </div>
            <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              We also write policies for tenants and niche personal lines. Your landlord's insurance only covers the building structure—it does not cover your personal belongings, furniture, or guest injuries inside your apartment.
            </p>
            <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3 pt-1">
              <a href="/quote?type=renters" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-accent-gold hover:text-accent-gold-hover transition-colors">
                Request Renters Quote
                <svg class="w-4 h-4" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
                  <path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M13.5 4.5 21 12m0 0-7.5 7.5M21 12H3" />
                </svg>
              </a>
              <a href="/personal/renters" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-xs font-semibold text-accent hover:underline">
                Explore In-Depth Renters Guide & FAQs →
              </a>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="lg:col-span-8 bg-bg-secondary p-8 rounded-lg border border-border-subtle space-y-6">
            <div class="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-6 text-xs text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              <div>
                <h4 class="font-bold text-text-primary mb-1">Renters Insurance</h4>
                <p>Covers replacement of clothing, computers, and furniture in the event of theft or fire. Includes tenant liability in case of minor accidents inside the rented unit.</p>
              </div>
              <div>
                <h4 class="font-bold text-text-primary mb-1">Pet Insurance</h4>
                <p>Accident and illness plans for dogs and cats. Covers veterinary visits, surgeries, and prescriptions so you never have to make health decisions based on expense.</p>
              </div>

            <p class="font-medium text-text-primary">
              A Associated Insurance Agency (AIA) é uma corretora de seguros independente fundada em 2016, com filiais físicas em Danbury, Watertown e Bridgeport, Connecticut. A AIA faz parceria com seguradoras líderes para oferecer coberturas personalizadas residenciais, comerciais e de responsabilidade, com corretores multilíngues fluentes em inglês, espanhol, português e turco.
            </p>

            </p>
            <p>
              Como uma agência independente de serviço completo, não trabalhamos para nenhuma companhia de seguros específica. Em vez disso, temos parcerias com uma ampla rede de seguradoras mais bem avaliadas da região e do país. Essa independência nos permite pesquisar, comparar apólices e apresentar a você opções que oferecem a melhor cobertura com as taxas mais baixas disponíveis no mercado.

              Se você estiver comprando sua primeira casa, adicionando um novo veículo à sua apólice familiar ou gerenciando uma empresa local em crescimento, nossos agentes experientes dedicam tempo para analisar seus riscos e combiná-lo com opções que protegem o que é mais importante.
            </p>
            <p>
              Para melhor atender às nossas diversas comunidades de Connecticut, nossa equipe é totalmente multilíngue. Temos o orgulho de oferecer consultoria, atendimento a apólices e suporte a sinistros em inglês, espanhol, português e turco, garantindo que o idioma nunca seja uma barreira para obter a proteção que você precisa.

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">O seguro de carro pessoal cobre o uso para o trabalho em Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Não. Quase todas as apólices pessoais contêm cláusulas estritas de exclusão de uso comercial. Se você ou um funcionário sofrer um acidente transportando ferramentas, materiais ou fazendo entregas, a seguradora pessoal negará a cobertura, deixando sua empresa desprotegida contra processos milionários.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">O que é a cobertura de Veículos Alugados e Não Próprios (HNOA)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              A cobertura HNOA protege sua empresa quando colaboradores utilizam seus próprios carros pessoais para tarefas da firma (como comprar materiais, ir ao banco ou atender clientes) ou quando a empresa aluga vans temporárias. Ela blinda o patrimônio da empresa caso os limites do motorista se esgotem.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">O seguro comercial de veículos cobre as ferramentas deixadas no carro?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              A apólice de auto comercial cobre apenas a estrutura do veículo e peças permanentemente instaladas. Para proteger ferramentas elétricas, máquinas e materiais guardados na caçamba ou baú, a AIA anexa uma extensão de 'Inland Marine' para equipamentos móveis.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Quais limites de responsabilidade são recomendados em Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Os limites mínimos da lei estadual (CGS § 14-112) de $25k/$50k/$25k são muito baixos para proteger uma empresa. Veículos comerciais e frotas contratam limites combinados (CSL) de no mínimo $500,000 a $1,000,000, comumente acompanhados de uma apólice Umbrella.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>

              As despesas com advogados de defesa são pagas além do limite da apólice na maioria dos contratos, preservando o valor total de indenização.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent">Perguntas Frequentes</h2>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">Dúvidas comuns sobre o seguro de Responsabilidade Geral em Connecticut.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="space-y-4">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">O seguro de Responsabilidade Civil Geral é obrigatório por lei em Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Embora a legislação de Connecticut não o exija de forma universal para todas as empresas, ele é indispensável na prática. Proprietários de imóveis comerciais exigem apólice antes de assinar contratos de locação, empreiteiros gerais exigem prova de cobertura (COI) para permitir o trabalho em obras e as ordens de licenciamento exigem seguro ativo.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Com que rapidez a Associated Insurance Agency emite um Certificado de Seguro (COI)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Para segurados ativos, a Associated Insurance Agency emite Certificados de Seguro padrão ACORD 25 no mesmo dia, frequentemente em minutos. Isso permite que empreiteiros e prestadores de serviços fechem contratos e acessem locais de trabalho sem atrasos.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Quais são os limites padrão de apólice em Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              O padrão adotado no mercado de Connecticut é de $1,000,000 por ocorrência e $2,000,000 de limite agregado total ($1M/$2M). Empreiteiros com contratos maiores costumam contratar apólices Umbrella Comercial para elevar a proteção para $5,000,000 ou mais.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Qual é a diferença entre uma apólice isolada e um pacote BOP?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Uma apólice avulsa cobre estritamente processos judiciais de terceiros por lesões corporais e danos materiais. A Apólice de Dono de Negócio (BOP) reúne Responsabilidade Geral, Seguro de Propriedade Comercial e Lucros Cessantes em um pacote integrado com tarifas reduzidas.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

Pela Lei de Compensação de Trabalhadores de Connecticut (CGS § 31-284), qualquer empresa que contrate um ou mais trabalhadores (sejam em tempo integral, meio período ou temporários) deve manter uma apólice ativa. A falta do seguro acarreta ordens imediatas de paralisação e multas de no mínimo $500 por dia.

Caso subcontratados sem seguro tenham trabalhado para você, a seguradora cobrará esse custo de sua empresa. Na AIA, orientamos sua gestão para evitar surpresas no acerto final.

            <p>Aplicativos móveis ou aparelhos opcionais que acompanham quilometragem e frenagens suaves geram descontos de até 30%.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="space-y-1">
            <strong class="text-accent block">Bons Estudantes e Cursos de Direção</strong>
            <p>Descontos para estudantes com boas notas, jovens que estudam longe sem carro e motoristas de 60+ que concluírem cursos estaduais de direção defensiva.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

        <div class="text-center space-y-2">
          <h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-accent">Perguntas Frequentes</h2>
          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">Respostas diretas sobre seguro de automóvel e veículos recreativos em Connecticut.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="space-y-4">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Quais são os limites mínimos obrigatórios de seguro auto em Connecticut (CGS § 14-112)?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Pela legislação de Connecticut (CGS § 14-112), todo condutor deve manter cobertura mínima de responsabilidade civil de $25,000 por lesão corporal individual, $50,000 por acidente e $25,000 para danos materiais (25/50/25), além de cobertura idêntica para motoristas não segurados ou com seguro insuficiente (UM/UIM).
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Por que os limites mínimos da lei são insuficientes para a maioria dos motoristas?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              O valor médio de um carro novo hoje passa de $48,000. Se você provocar um acidente com perda total de um carro recente, o teto de $25,000 para danos materiais deixa uma diferença de mais de $20,000 que você terá de pagar do próprio bolso. Se os custos médicos dos feridos ultrapassarem os $50,000 da apólice, eles podem acionar a justiça contra suas economias e sua casa. Recomendamos limites de pelo menos 100/300/100 ou 250/500/100.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Qual é a diferença entre cobertura de Colisão e Compreensiva em Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              A cobertura de Colisão paga pelo conserto ou reposição do seu carro se você bater em outro veículo, em uma defensa metálica ou capotar. A cobertura Compreensiva protege contra sinistros fora de uma colisão: atropelamento de animais (veados), pedras no para-brisa, furto, vandalismo, incêndio e galhos caídos durante tempestades.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Posso segurar meu motorhome, trailer ou camper na mesma apólice?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              A maioria das seguradoras exige uma apólice especializada para veículos recreativos em vez de incluí-los na apólice de carro comum. Podemos emitir as duas apólices com a mesma companhia para aproveitar descontos e cobrir responsabilidade em áreas de camping, reboque e pertences pessoais a bordo.
            </p>
          </div>

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Qual é a diferença entre custo de reconstrução e valor de mercado?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              O valor de mercado é o preço pago por um comprador, englobando o terreno e a localização. O custo de reconstrução é o valor em materiais e mão de obra necessário para reconstruir o imóvel do zero. Como os custos de mão de obra e construção em Connecticut estão entre os mais altos do país, o custo para reconstruir costuma diferir bastante do valor de mercado ou da avaliação de impostos.

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

A cobertura contra inundações exige uma apólice à parte pelo Programa Nacional de Seguros contra Inundação (NFIP) ou por seguradoras privadas, que emitimos junto com a apólice do seu imóvel.

            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Quanto posso economizar ao combinar o seguro da casa e do carro?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">

            <p>A maioria das seguradoras exige $250,000 / $500,000 de danos corporais e $100,000 de danos materiais, ou limite único combinado de $500,000.</p>

          <p class="text-sm text-text-secondary">Dúvidas sobre o seguro guarda-chuva em Connecticut.</p>

        <div class="space-y-4">
          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">O que é uma apólice Guarda-Chuva (Umbrella) e como ela funciona?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Uma apólice Guarda-Chuva (Personal Umbrella) adiciona cobertura de responsabilidade civil acima dos limites de suas apólices normais de carro, residência ou embarcação. Quando um processo ou indenização consome os limites básicos, a apólice guarda-chuva cobre o saldo restante até o limite contratado ($1,000,000 a $5,000,000 ou mais).
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Quem precisa de um seguro guarda-chuva em Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Qualquer pessoa com patrimônio a proteger—como imóvel próprio, poupança, aposentadoria ou renda futura—se beneficia da apólice guarda-chuva. Processos judiciais afetam famílias de todos os perfis financeiros. Riscos frequentes incluem motoristas jovens, piscinas, animais de estimação e imóveis alugados.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Quanto custa uma apólice guarda-chuva de $1,000,000 em Connecticut?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              Como a cobertura atua apenas após o esgotamento das apólices primárias, o custo é relativamente baixo. Uma apólice de $1,000,000 costuma variar entre $150 e $300 por ano (cerca de $15 a $25 por mês). Cada milhão adicional custa proporcionalmente menos.
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-white p-6 rounded-xl border border-border-subtle shadow-sm space-y-2">
            <h3 class="text-base font-bold text-accent">Quais são os limites básicos exigidos para poder contratar a guarda-chuva?</h3>
            <p class="text-xs sm:text-sm text-text-secondary leading-relaxed">
              As seguradoras exigem limites mínimos nas apólices primárias: normalmente $250,000/$500,000 de responsabilidade por danos corporais no automóvel e $300,000 a $500,000 de responsabilidade na residência. A Associated Insurance Agency alinha suas apólices para evitar lacunas na cobertura.
            </p>
          </div>
